segments.say: Lesson 21. Fine-tuning versus rag versus Prompting. S F T, lora/Q lora, preference tuning (R L H F/D P O), distillation, and a decision framework.

Fine-tuning means training an existing model a bit more on your own examples to change its behaviour (style, format, a specialised task). For adding knowledge, rag is usually the better tool. Here is an analogy. Hiring an experienced chef (pretrained model) and training them for two weeks in your restaurant's style (fine-tuning), versus. just giving them your recipe book each day (rag).

Why does this matter? "Should we fine-tune or use rag?" is one of the most common A I-engineering questions. A few key words. S F T: Supervised fine-tuning on input leads to ideal output pairs. lora: Train tiny add-on matrices instead of all weights. Q lora: lora on a 4-bit compressed model, so it fits one G P U. D P O / R L H F: Training on preferred versus rejected answers. Distillation: A big model teaches a small one.

segments.sec: Watch: Which lever do I pull?
segments.say: Which lever do I pull. Your L L M app isn't good enough. Fine-tuning is not the first answer. Diagnose what kind of problem it is.

segments.sec: Watch: Which lever do I pull?
segments.say: Knowledge problem (private, fresh or large data) leads to rag. Fine-tuning is a poor, expensive way to inject facts, and they go stale.

segments.sec: Watch: Which lever do I pull?
segments.say: Behaviour problem (format, tone, task style) leads to first try prompting plus few-shot plus structured output.

segments.sec: Watch: Which lever do I pull?
segments.say: If prompting plateaus and you have hundreds to thousands of quality examples leads to fine-tune, usually parameter-efficient (lora).

segments.sec: Watch: Which lever do I pull?
segments.say: Cost or latency problem leads to distill: use a big model's outputs to fine-tune a small, fast model for your narrow task.

segments.sec: Watch: Which lever do I pull?
segments.say: They combine: rag for knowledge plus a fine-tuned model for behaviour is common in mature systems.
lora in one picture. Full fine-tuning updates every weight. That means huge G P U memory and a full model copy per task.
lora: freeze W and learn two tiny low-rank matrices whose product is the update. Rank 8 leads to ~0.4% of the parameters.
Q lora: quantize the frozen base to 4-bit and train lora adapters on top. You can fine-tune big models on a single G P U.
Adapters are megabytes. One base model can serve many swappable adapters, one per task or customer.

Fine-tuning flavours. Continued pre-training: more raw domain text. Expensive, rare for app teams. S F T (supervised fine-tuning): instruction leads to ideal response pairs. Teaches format, style and task behaviour. Preference tuning: R L H F (reward model plus P P O) or the simpler D P O: train on chosen versus rejected answers. P E F T: lora / Q lora adapters instead of full weights. Distillation: a big "teacher" generates data and a small "student" learns it.

Requirements & risks. Clean, representative data (quality beats quantity), plus a held-out eval set. Catastrophic forgetting: the model loses general skills. Mix in general data, keep lora rank modest. Maintenance: re-tune whenever the base model upgrades. Hosting: open-weight models need serving infrastructure; vendor fine-tuning has lock-in.

Say it in the interview. "rag for knowledge, fine-tuning for behaviour. I exhaust prompting, few-shot and structured outputs first. If quality plateaus and I have a few thousand curated examples, I'd do lora S F T, possibly D P O on preference pairs, and evaluate against a held-out set and general benchmarks to catch forgetting. For cost I'd distill into a smaller model.".

Let's compare. Adds new knowledge: limited by context, best, poorly, goes stale. Changes style / format: often enough,, best. Data needed: few examples, documents, 100s–1000s labelled pairs. Update speed: minutes, re-index docs, retrain. Cost: lowest, medium, highest upfront. Citations / explainability: —,,.

A likely interview question: rag or fine-tuning? A strong answer: rag when the problem is knowledge (private, fresh, citable). Fine-tuning when it's behaviour (format, style, specialized task) and prompting has plateaued. Often both.
That's it for Fine-tuning versus rag versus Prompting. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
